newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Irish, Finnish EMU chances seen slumping. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Irish, Finnish EMU chances seen slumping. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]

text.p: EMU watchers have written down Ireland and Finland's chances of becoming founder members of a single European currency because of the Euro-sceptic stance of their neighbours, according to a Reuters survey published on Thursday.
In the Reuters EMU barometer for April, which assesses the likelihood of EMU starting on time, 17 out of 38 contributors gave a 100 percent likelihood of Finland and Ireland being founder members.
(Corrects to make clear that the analysts were asked to forecast whether nations would be 100 percent certain to join EMU from the start.)

The forecasts, which were gathered on April 14 and 15, showed the two countries' chances of early entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU) were being hampered because of the near certainty that their major trading partners, Britain and Sweden, would remain outside EMU.

"It will be difficult for them to join if their major trading partners, Sweden and the UK, are adamant they will not be in the first wave. Their currencies and economies are tied together," said Daniel Gros, senior research fellow at the Centre for Economic Policy Studies in Belgium.

Britain, where both major parties campaigning for a May 1 election are lukewarm about early EMU entry, and Sweden, where there is strong political opposition to EMU, are both thought highly unlikely to join the single currency club from the beginning.
In the Reuters barometer, no contributor forecast Britain as 100 percent likely to join from the start. Only one forecaster gave Sweden a 100 percent chance of being a founder member.
